summary: Diagnostics represented-set hardening still lacks concrete Instance binding. PhysicsLabRealizer.isRepresented(entityId) proves only that the private representation map has a non-nil entry consistent with F0/F2 authority; it does not prove that the direct Workspace child currently being enumerated by PhysicsLabStudioDiagnostics is that exact runtime-owned Instance. A stale destroyed map entry plus a substituted child carrying the same canonical WorldEntityId/fidelity can therefore satisfy unique-id, represented-count, and boolean membership checks while diagnostics publishes evidence for an unowned substitute.
evidence: src/server/PhysicsLab/PhysicsLabRealizer.luau stores the actual physical views in the private representations map, but RealizedLab exposes only isRepresented(entityId): boolean; that function computes representations[entityId] ~= nil and does not compare a candidate Instance to the stored map value or verify that stored value remains parented to the owned lab model.

Active recovery PR #327 strengthens diagnostics with unique WorldEntityIds, lab.isRepresented(id) membership, and authoritative UNRENDERED_RepresentedCount equality. Those checks prove cardinality and ID membership but cannot bind an enumerated child to the concrete Instance owned by the representation map.

A one-for-one substitution can preserve all three proposed predicates: externally destroy the real child without changing the private map, parent a substitute child under the lab with the same WorldEntityId/fidelity, and keep the represented count unchanged. The boolean map membership remains true because the stale map reference is still non-nil, while diagnostics observes the substitute.

Search across current diagnostics PRs found no separate Instance-identity binding fix; #327 explicitly claims represented-count + membership hardening, while #301 covers count completeness and lifecycle ordering and #304 covers failure-atomicity/cycle-input documentation.
